summary: Platform sub-package ships opaque Go binary with websocket-driven PTY remote-shell capability
details: The tarball ships a single 7 MB Mach-O x86_64 Go executable at bin/ccfly-setup with no source, no build system, no README, and placeholder metadata. The binary statically links github.com/creack/pty and github.com/gorilla/websocket alongside internal packages github.com/ccfly/rescue and github.com/ccfly/rescue/cmd/setup, and embeds ws:// / wss:// URL literals (fragments 'ws://ccfly', 'wss://', 'http://approveccfly-*/redeem', 'cc.hn') plus a 'latest.zshrc.ccfly' shell-init reference. The combination of a PTY spawn primitive, a websocket transport, and shell-init file handling is the shape of a websocket-driven remote-shell agent: a remote party connecting to the embedded endpoint can drive an interactive shell on the host that runs the binary, and can seed a persistent zsh startup file. The npm package itself declares no lifecycle scripts, no main, and no bin, so `npm install` of this platform sub-package alone does not execute the binary; a parent @ccfly orchestrator package invokes it. Package self-describes as a guided-install helper but ships remote-shell primitives rather than installer logic.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
